tools.name: rotate_model
tools.description: Orbit the camera around the model on screen. Positive yawDegrees moves the camera to the right around the model, negative to the left. Positive pitchDegrees moves the camera up to look down on it. The state's yawDegrees and pitchDegrees say where the camera is now.

yawDegrees.description: Degrees to orbit left or right, from -360 to 360.

pitchDegrees.description: Degrees to orbit up or down, from -80 to 80. Leave out to keep the height.

tools.name: zoom
tools.description: Move the camera closer to or farther from what it looks at. factor 1.3 moves about 30 percent closer, 0.7 about 30 percent farther. The state's zoom runs from 0 (farthest) to 1 (closest).

factor.description: Above 1 zooms in, below 1 zooms out, from 0.3 to 3.

tools.name: zoom_to_part
tools.description: Move the camera to one labeled part, make it glow, and dim the others. label must be one of the state's labels.

label.description: A label from the state's labels.

tools.name: reset_view
tools.description: Show the whole model again from the starting angle, with no part highlighted, assembled and closed.

tools.name: explode_view
tools.description: Pull the model's parts apart from its center so each one shows, or put them back. amount 0 is assembled, 1 is fully apart.

tools.name: set_inside_view
tools.description: Cut away the half of the outer shell nearest the camera so the parts inside show, or close it again.

open.description: true cuts the shell open, false closes it.

tools.name: set_control
tools.description: Change one number of the simulation on screen and put it back at its start, without running it. The controls are: angle (Launch angle, 5 to 85 deg); speed (Launch speed, 5 to 30 m/s). The state's controls hold each one's current value. Use the control's name and a value in its unit.

name.description: The name of one control from the description.

value.description: The new value in the control's unit. The page clamps it to the control's range.

tools.name: set_labels
tools.description: Show or hide the part labels and their leader lines on the simulation. They are hidden at first, because they cover the setup, so show them only when the learner asks for labels or asks what the parts are. The state's labelsAreShown says whether they show now.

visible.description: true shows the labels, false hides them.

tools.name: run_simulation
tools.description: Play the simulation on screen once from its start with the current controls. It takes a few seconds, and the state's readouts hold the result when it ends.

tools.name: answer_with_screen
tools.description: Answer a question about what is on screen, using a screenshot. Use it for questions and for anything no other tool can do, not for changing the view.

tools.name: build_new_scene
tools.description: Build a 3D view now, which pauses the video and takes about 20 seconds. Use it when the learner asks to show, see, or render something in 3D, such as "show me this in 3D" over a video, where a famous real place appears as its real 3D scan, and when they want a different model or something not on screen yet. When they ask to build, make, or create a 3D model, use build_model_in_background instead, if it is offered. When they want to try it, play with it, or simulate it, use build_simulation instead. Never use it to turn, zoom, or open the model already showing.

asQuiz.description: true when they asked to be quizzed or tested on it.

tools.name: build_simulation
tools.description: Build a playable experiment of what the video or screen shows, such as a ball launched at an angle, a lever, or a pendulum, with sliders and a Run button. It builds in the background for about 30 to 40 seconds while the video keeps playing, and then rises out of the video, or waits until the learner asks to see it if something else is on screen. Use it when the learner says let me try it, let me play with it, can I try it, or simulate this, and no simulation is on screen yet. When one is on screen, use set_control and run_simulation instead. Your confirmation is a few plain words that it has started, such as "setting it up", never that it is done.

tools.name: pop_out
tools.description: Lift the subject of the video frame or the largest picture in Chrome's front tab out in 3D with its parts labeled. Use it only when they say pop this out or pop it out. It pauses a playing video by itself.

tools.name: animate_picture
tools.description: Lift the video frame or the largest picture in Chrome's front tab out in 3D and show what flows through it as moving streams, such as air through an engine or blood through a heart. Over a pop-out already on screen, it animates that one. Use it only when the learner says animate this, make it move, or make it flow. A painting is left as the artist made it, and the app says so. Use answer_with_screen when they ask how to animate something in another app. It pauses a playing video by itself.

tools.name: close_scene
tools.description: Close the 3D scene on screen. A paused video plays again.

tools.name: explain_part
tools.description: Say what one labeled part does, while the camera turns to it. label must be one of the scene state's labels. Use it, not answer_with_screen, for a question about a labeled part, such as "what does the valve do" or "what is the crankshaft for".

tools.name: pause_video
tools.description: Pause the video in Chrome's front tab.

tools.name: play_video
tools.description: Play the video in Chrome's front tab.

tools.name: seek_relative
tools.description: Move the video in Chrome's front tab forward (positive seconds) or back (negative seconds).

seconds.description: Seconds to move, negative to go back.

tools.name: seek_to_time
tools.description: Move the video in Chrome's front tab to a time, in seconds from the start.

seconds.description: Seconds from the start of the video.

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: Set how fast the video in Chrome's front tab plays. 1 is normal speed.

tools.name: find_moment
tools.description: Search the video's captions for where something is said, without moving the video. Returns up to 3 moments, best match first, with their times. Use it when the learner asks when or where something is said, wants a particular mention such as the last or the second one, or says seek_to_moment landed in the wrong place. Then call seek_to_time with the time you pick. To go straight to the best match, use seek_to_moment.

query.description: A few words that would be said at that moment.

tools.name: seek_to_moment
tools.description: Move the video in Chrome's front tab to the caption line that best matches query, in one step. It lands on the single best match, never on the first or last mention. Use it when the learner says go to, go back to, or jump to where something is said or explained, such as "go back to where he explains the gills". Put the words they would hear in query. Call every other tool they asked for in the same reply, because this tool needs no result before the next one and tools in one reply run in the order you call them. "Go to where he explains the gills and back up ten seconds" is seek_to_moment and then seek_relative with -10, and "jump to the part about the teeth and pop it out" is seek_to_moment and then pop_out. When they want the first, last, or another particular mention, or only ask when something is said, use find_moment, and then seek_to_time if they want to go there.

query.description: A few words that would be said at that moment.

tools.name: end_quiz
tools.description: Stop the video quiz.

tools.name: make_study_guide
tools.description: Write a Notion study guide for the YouTube video in Chrome's front tab. It runs in the background for up to a minute while the video keeps playing, and a chip under the cursor shows when the page is ready, with nothing spoken. Use it when the learner asks for a study guide, notes, or a summary page in Notion. Put an extra wish, such as only the part about the engine, in focus. Your confirmation is a few plain words that it has started, such as "writing it now", never that it is done.

focus.description: An extra wish for the guide, such as only the part about the engine. Leave it out when they made none.

tools.name: revise_study_guide
tools.description: Change the study guide already written for this video, such as making it shorter, adding detail on one part, or adding a section. The new page replaces the old one in Notion and is written in the background. Put what to change in instruction, in the learner's words. Your confirmation is a few plain words that it has started, such as "updating it now", never that it is done.

instruction.description: What to change about the guide, in the learner's words.

tools.name: open_study_guide
tools.description: Open this video's study guide page in Notion. Use it when the learner asks to see, open, or go to the guide, and when they ask for a new study guide, since this video already has one. In that case your confirmation says they already have a guide for this video and you are opening it.

tools.name: build_model_in_background
tools.description: Build a 3D model of what the video shows in the background, for about 20 seconds, while the video keeps playing. When it is ready it rises out of the video, or waits until the learner asks for it if something else is on screen. Use it when the learner asks to build, make, or create a 3D model, such as "build me a 3D model of this engine", or asks for one while they keep watching. Use build_new_scene instead when they ask to show, see, or render something in 3D right now, and for a famous real place, whose real 3D scan only build_new_scene shows. Put what to build in whatToBuild, in the learner's words. Your confirmation is a few plain words that it has started, such as "starting the model", never that it is done.

whatToBuild.description: What to build, in the learner's words, such as this jet engine.

tools.name: show_ready_model
tools.description: Show the 3D model or experiment built in the background, which is ready and waiting. It pauses the video and rises out of it. Use it, never a new build, when the learner asks to see, show, or open the model or the experiment, such as "show me the model" or "let me see it".

tools.name: start_background_task
tools.description: Hand a task to a background agent that works on its own for a minute or two while the learner keeps watching. It can search the web, read this video's captions, look at the video, and write a Notion page. Use it when the learner asks you to find out, look up, research, compare, check, or collect something that needs more than a quick answer from the screen, such as "find out how this compares to the first booster catch". Use make_study_guide for a study guide of this video, and build_model_in_background for a 3D model. Put the task in goal, in the learner's words, with what this or that refers to on screen. Your confirmation is a few plain words that it has started, such as "looking into it", never that it is done.

goal.description: The task in the learner's words, with what it refers to on screen.

tools.name: hear_task_answer
tools.description: Say what the background task agent found. Use it when the learner asks what it found, what the answer was, or to hear the result.

tools.name: record_guess
tools.description: Record the learner's guess to the simulation's prediction question, the scene state's predictionQuestion, which unlocks the Run button and the dashed path. Use it for any answer to that question, even a short or unsure one, such as "60 goes farther", "they tie", or "the first one". Do not use it for a command such as changing a control or running it. Put the guess in guess, in the learner's words. Your confirmation is a few plain words, such as "got it, now try it".

guess.description: The learner's guess, in their words.

tools.name: answer_approval
tools.description: Answer the request a background agent is waiting on, which asks the learner to allow one action. The scene state's approvalWaiting names the kind of action, never the action itself. Use it only when the learner answers that request: yes, sure, go ahead, or do it allows it (approved true), and no, don't, stop, or cancel declines it (approved false). Set always true only when they say always or always allow it. Do not use it for any other command. Your confirmation is two plain words, such as "allowed it" or "declined it".

approved.description: true to allow the action, false to decline it.

always.description: true only when the learner said always, so the agent need not ask again for this tool. Never true when approved is false.

tools.name: design_theme
tools.description: Open the Theme Studio, a card with three whole theme ideas, or change the ideas already on it. A theme is a cursor, its colors, its agent token colors, and its sounds, and it can use the picture the learner points at. Use it when the learner asks to change, make, design, or customize their theme, and for any wish about how the cursor looks, moves, or sounds while the card is open, such as "two, but make the cursor a star that spins while it thinks". While the card is open, a new vibe or subject, such as "something totally different, like the ocean", is a wish for new theme ideas, never a 3D scene. Put the wish in request, in the learner's words. Set basedOnIdea, from 1 to 3, when they name one idea on the card to change. Set fromPicture true when they say this picture, this image, or this photo, or false when they drop the picture, and leave it out otherwise. It takes several seconds, and the card and a spoken line say the result, so a confirmation is never spoken. Never use it to pick, save, or close.

request.description: What the learner wants, in their words, such as something cozy for night.

basedOnIdea.description: The idea on the card the change applies to, from 1 to 3. Leave it out when no one idea is named.

fromPicture.description: true to design from the largest picture in Chrome's front tab, false to drop the picture the card has. Leave it out otherwise.

tools.name: pick_theme_idea
tools.description: Highlight one of the ideas on the Theme Studio card and try it on the real cursor. Use it when the learner says just a number or names an idea, such as "two" or "the star one". number is the idea's number on the card, from 1 to 3. Your confirmation is a few plain words, such as "trying two".

number.description: The idea's number on the card, from 1 to 3.

tools.name: save_theme
tools.description: Save the highlighted idea on the Theme Studio card as the learner's theme and apply it. Use it when they say save it, use it, I'll take it, or perfect. When they name an idea with it, such as "save two", call pick_theme_idea first. Your confirmation is a few plain words, such as "saved it".

tools.name: close_theme_studio
tools.description: Close the Theme Studio card and keep the old theme. Use it for never mind, cancel, close it, or forget it while the card is open. Your confirmation is a few plain words, such as "kept your old theme".
